title: Holding On: The Latch
endLine: The phosphate switches myosin on; slow release lets force outlast it.

scenes.tts: The first film said force follows the balance of kinase and phosphatase. That holds while force is being built. Keep a strip of artery muscle stimulated. Phosphorylation rises, then falls back toward low values. Yet force stays near its peak. What is holding the load?
scenes.narration: The first film said force follows the balance of kinase and phosphatase. That holds while force is being built. Keep a strip of artery muscle stimulated. Phosphorylation rises, then falls back toward low values. Yet force stays near its peak. What is holding the load?
scenes.caption: The first film said force follows the balance of kinase and phosphatase. That holds while force is being built. Keep a strip of artery muscle stimulated. Phosphorylation rises, then falls back toward low values. Yet force stays near its peak. What is holding the load?
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's colour map: YELLOW calcium; GREEN myosin light-chain kinase (MLCK); RED myosin light-chain phosphatase (MLCP); GOLD round 'P' badge = a phosphate on the light chain; BLUE myosin heads, thick filament and force; GREY actin and structure. NEW in this film: MAGENTA = latch bridge (an attached head with no phosphate). ONE WORLD, kept all film, 16:9: TOP 55% of the frame, a long GREY actin filament spans the width; below it a BLUE thick filament bar with six BLUE myosin heads reaching up toward the actin. BOTTOM-LEFT, the first film's seesaw, shrunk: GREEN 'MLCK kinase' on the left end, RED 'MLCP phosphatase' on the right end, YELLOW 'calcium' chip above the kinase end. BOTTOM-RIGHT, a small time plot, x axis 'time' (no numbers), two traces: GOLD 'phosphorylation' and BLUE 'force', with a tag 'schematic'. On the link-back sentences, the seesaw tips kinase-down as GOLD P badges land on four of six heads, the heads grab the actin and stroke, and both traces climb together (tag 'force being built'). On 'stimulated', the YELLOW chip stays lit. On 'falls back toward low values', the GOLD trace drops to about a quarter of its peak while GOLD badges pop off three heads; those heads stay attached to the actin. On 'near its peak', the BLUE trace keeps a flat plateau just under its peak. On the question, large white text above the actin: 'What holds the load?' The attached heads quiver slightly under tension.
Title 'Holding On: The Latch' fades in for 2 s above the actin while the question text fades out. The heads keep a slight quiver; the BLUE force trace extends flat; the GOLD trace stays low.

scenes.tts: If force simply tracked phosphorylation, it would follow it down. In 1988, Hai and Murphy proposed a kinetic model. Each myosin head is phosphorylated or not, and attached or not: four states. Kinase and phosphatase act on heads whether or not they are bound.
scenes.narration: If force simply tracked phosphorylation, it would follow it down. In 1988, Hai and Murphy proposed a kinetic model. Each myosin head is phosphorylated or not, and attached or not: four states. Kinase and phosphatase act on heads whether or not they are bound.
scenes.caption: If force simply tracked phosphorylation, it would follow it down. In 1988, Hai and Murphy proposed a kinetic model. Each myosin head is phosphorylated or not, and attached or not: four states. Kinase and phosphatase act on heads whether or not they are bound.
scenes.visual: On 'follow it down', a dashed BLUE ghost trace peels off the force plateau and slides down along the GOLD trace, then fades: the outcome that did not happen. Tag at top left: 'Hai and Murphy, 1988 (model)'. Camera eases in on the head row. Four of the six heads step forward and freeze in a 2 x 2 arrangement beneath the actin, one per state, each with a label of 2 words: 'P, detached' (badge, head away from actin), 'P, attached' (badge, head on actin), 'no P, detached', 'no P, attached'. On 'act on heads', a GREEN arrow from the seesaw's kinase end adds a GOLD badge to a detached head AND to an attached head; a RED arrow from the phosphatase end removes a badge from each, the same way. No molecular structures: heads are simple BLUE rounded shapes.

scenes.tts: So the balance still sets how many heads carry a phosphate. But a head that loses its phosphate while attached does not release at once. It becomes a latch bridge, and its slow detachment is the rate-limiting step.
scenes.narration: So the balance still sets how many heads carry a phosphate. But a head that loses its phosphate while attached does not release at once. It becomes a latch bridge, and its slow detachment is the rate-limiting step.
scenes.caption: So the balance still sets how many heads carry a phosphate. But a head that loses its phosphate while attached does not release at once. It becomes a latch bridge, and its slow detachment is the rate-limiting step.
scenes.visual: The 2 x 2 heads return to the row. On 'the balance still sets', the small seesaw rocks and the count of GOLD badges on the row follows it. Focus on one attached head with a badge, pulling on the actin. On 'loses its phosphate while attached', the RED phosphatase removes its GOLD badge; the head does NOT let go. It turns MAGENTA and is labelled 'latch bridge'. On 'slow detachment', a small clock face beside it ticks slowly; a neighbouring BLUE head with a badge (cycling) attaches, strokes and releases twice in the same time while the MAGENTA head finally lets go once, then reattaches only after picking up a new badge. Tag 'rate-limiting step' beside the clock.

scenes.tts: Here is the one idea. The phosphate switches heads on; attached heads that lose it let go slowly. So force can outlast the phosphate, while cycling and its A T P cost fall.
scenes.narration: Here is the one idea. The phosphate switches heads on; attached heads that lose it let go slowly. So force can outlast the phosphate, while cycling and its ATP cost fall.
scenes.caption: Here is the one idea. The phosphate switches heads on; attached heads that lose it let go slowly. So force can outlast the phosphate, while cycling and its ATP cost fall.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full world. Replay the hook as one transformation: GOLD badges land, heads attach and stroke, both traces rise; then badges come off, and each attached head that loses its badge turns MAGENTA and stays on the actin. Most attached heads are now MAGENTA. The GOLD trace sits low; the BLUE force trace stays on its plateau. On 'switches heads on', the GOLD badges flash; on 'lets go slowly', the MAGENTA heads glow. On 'cycling and its ATP cost fall', a small counter of stroking heads labelled 'cycling' drops from 4 to 1 and a small BLUE meter labelled 'ATP use' falls (schematic, no numbers). Large text under the actin: 'force outlasts the phosphate'.

scenes.tts: Take one illustrative run of the model. A steady seventeen percent phosphorylation held about eighty-six percent of the force held at sixty-seven percent. Most of it sat on latch bridges. The figure depends on the constants chosen. The slow release is a model assumption, not a structure anyone has imaged.
scenes.narration: Take one illustrative run of the model. A steady 17 percent phosphorylation held about 86 percent of the force held at 67 percent. Most of it sat on latch bridges. The figure depends on the constants chosen. The slow release is a model assumption, not a structure anyone has imaged.
scenes.caption: Take one illustrative run of the model. A steady 17 percent phosphorylation held about 86 percent of the force held at 67 percent. Most of it sat on latch bridges. The figure depends on the constants chosen. The slow release is a model assumption, not a structure anyone has imaged.
scenes.visual: The time plot at bottom right transforms into two BLUE bars, tagged 'illustrative model run'. Left bar labelled '67% phosphorylated', height 1.00 (reference force). Right bar labelled '17% phosphorylated', height 0.86 of the left bar, with '≈86%' above it. Bar heights are computed from these lesson values. Meanwhile the head row matches each bar by simple counting: for 67%, four of the six heads carry GOLD badges (4/6 = 67%); then the badges drop to one of six (1/6 ≈ 17%) while five heads stay attached and four of them turn MAGENTA. On 'most of it sat on latch bridges', the right bar fills mostly MAGENTA from the bottom with a thin BLUE cap (schematic split). On 'depends on the constants chosen', the right bar's top wobbles between two faint marks, unlabelled. On 'not a structure anyone has imaged', a tag 'model, not imaged' appears beside the MAGENTA heads.

scenes.tts: Latch is not a state without A T P. Phosphorylated cross-bridges keep cycling, and latch bridges let go slowly. Nor is it rigor, the stiff state of a muscle out of A T P. Latch is economy, not shutdown.
scenes.narration: Latch is not a state without ATP. Phosphorylated cross-bridges keep cycling, and latch bridges let go slowly. Nor is it rigor, the stiff state of a muscle out of ATP. Latch is economy, not shutdown.
scenes.caption: Latch is not a state without ATP. Phosphorylated cross-bridges keep cycling, and latch bridges let go slowly. Nor is it rigor, the stiff state of a muscle out of ATP. Latch is economy, not shutdown.
scenes.visual: The bars shrink back into the time plot. In the head row: the one BLUE head with a GOLD badge keeps attaching and releasing; the MAGENTA heads release one at a time, slowly, and others take their place. A small chip 'ATP present' sits by the thick filament. On 'rigor', a faint grey copy of the head row appears beside the main row with every head frozen rigid on the actin and an empty fuel icon labelled 'rigor: no ATP'; it receives a RED cross and fades. On 'economy, not shutdown', the 'ATP use' meter from s04 sits low but not at zero, with a slow pulse.

scenes.tts: In 2022, Hammell and colleagues tested this on a few purified myosin molecules in a laser trap. Once force reached a plateau, they injected the phosphatase. Tonic myosin, from pig stomach, held force for a median of thirty-two seconds. Phasic myosin, from chicken gizzard, held for twenty-one.
scenes.narration: In 2022, Hammell and colleagues tested this on a few purified myosin molecules in a laser trap. Once force reached a plateau, they injected the phosphatase. Tonic myosin, from pig stomach, held force for a median of 32 seconds. Phasic myosin, from chicken gizzard, held for 21.
scenes.caption: In 2022, Hammell and colleagues tested this on a few purified myosin molecules in a laser trap. Once force reached a plateau, they injected the phosphatase. Tonic myosin, from pig stomach, held force for a median of 32 seconds. Phasic myosin, from chicken gizzard, held for 21.
scenes.visual: Same world, stripped down: the thick filament dissolves, leaving three BLUE heads with GOLD badges on a flat GREY surface labelled 'purified myosin'. The GREY actin filament stays above them; a WHITE bead appears on its right end inside a pale cone labelled 'laser trap'. Tag top left: 'Hammell et al., 2022'. The heads pull; the bead shifts right and the BLUE force trace in the plot rises to a plateau. On 'injected the phosphatase', a RED 'phosphatase' token drops in. The plot then transforms into a timeline: x axis 'seconds after injection', 0 to 40, ticks every 10. A solid BLUE bar grows from 0 to 32 labelled 'tonic (pig): 32 s'; below it a lighter BLUE bar grows from 0 to 21 labelled 'phasic (chicken): 21 s'. Small tag 'medians'. Bar lengths are drawn to scale from these values.

scenes.tts: But the phosphates were not timed on the trapped heads. A parallel assay put the midpoint of dephosphorylation near twenty-seven seconds. Which hold is the stronger evidence that force outlasted the phosphate?
scenes.narration: But the phosphates were not timed on the trapped heads. A parallel assay put the midpoint of dephosphorylation near 27 seconds. Which hold is the stronger evidence that force outlasted the phosphate?
scenes.caption: But the phosphates were not timed on the trapped heads. A parallel assay put the midpoint of dephosphorylation near 27 seconds. Which hold is the stronger evidence that force outlasted the phosphate?
scenes.visual: On 'not timed on the trapped heads', a small question mark sits over the GOLD badges on the trapped heads. On 'parallel assay', a small side panel labelled 'parallel assay' shows a GOLD bar draining. On 'near 27 seconds', a GOLD dashed vertical line drops onto the timeline at 27, labelled 'phosphate midpoint ≈27 s'. Both BLUE bars stay. Question card at top in white: 'Which hold is stronger evidence?'
Predict pause. The question card stays. The two BLUE bars and the GOLD dashed line at 27 hold still; the bead in the laser trap trembles slightly and the trapped heads quiver. No other change.

scenes.tts: The tonic hold. Only it outlasted that clock, so it is the more convincing. The phasic hold ended before the midpoint. And these were purified pig and chicken proteins, not an intact vessel.
scenes.narration: The tonic hold. Only it outlasted that clock, so it is the more convincing. The phasic hold ended before the midpoint. And these were purified pig and chicken proteins, not an intact vessel.
scenes.caption: The tonic hold. Only it outlasted that clock, so it is the more convincing. The phasic hold ended before the midpoint. And these were purified pig and chicken proteins, not an intact vessel.
scenes.visual: The question card dissolves. The part of the tonic bar beyond the GOLD line (27 to 32) glows MAGENTA, labelled 'held past the midpoint'. The phasic bar's end at 21 sits left of the GOLD line; a short bracket from 21 to 27 is labelled 'ended before'. On 'purified pig and chicken', a tag 'purified proteins, not a vessel' appears beside the laser trap.

scenes.tts: So once force is built, force and phosphorylation part ways. The balance sets how many heads switch on. Slow release decides how long the load stays up. That is how smooth muscle, above all tonic muscle, holds force cheaply.
scenes.narration: So once force is built, force and phosphorylation part ways. The balance sets how many heads switch on. Slow release decides how long the load stays up. That is how smooth muscle, above all tonic muscle, holds force cheaply.
scenes.caption: So once force is built, force and phosphorylation part ways. The balance sets how many heads switch on. Slow release decides how long the load stays up. That is how smooth muscle, above all tonic muscle, holds force cheaply.
scenes.visual: The trap fades and the full muscle world returns: actin, thick filament with six heads, the seesaw at bottom left, the time plot at bottom right with the GOLD and BLUE traces from the hook. On 'part ways', the GOLD trace falls while the BLUE trace holds its plateau, and the gap between them glows. On 'the balance sets', the seesaw tips and GOLD badges land on heads. On 'slow release', the MAGENTA latch bridges glow and hold the actin. On 'holds force cheaply', the small 'ATP use' meter sits low beside a full BLUE force gauge.

End card over the dimmed but still moving world (MAGENTA latch bridges holding the actin with a slight quiver, one BLUE head with a GOLD badge still cycling). Large white text, centred: 'The phosphate switches myosin on; slow release lets force outlast it.'
